title: Coldstart Bridge — quick reference & ephemeral runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact on-call bridge note for 'coldstart' incidents (full-service restart / mass eviction) where the primary goal is to restore traffic with minimal user-visible errors and a controlled cost profile. Treat as ephemeral: copy to a ticket and expand for postmortem.

Quick signature (what I look for first):
- System-wide: API error rate spike > 3% for > 2m OR p95 latency > 1200ms for > 3m.
- Infra signal: > 60% of GPU pods in Restarting/CrashLoopBackoff OR controller saw >= 25% pod churn in last 10m.
- Cost/Scale: autoscaler launching > 50 instances in 10m (possible runaway if warmup not bounded).

Fast-fail checklist (5 min triage):
1) Post to bridge: #oncall-inference, prefix message with [COLDSTART BRIDGE] and short summary. Include INF ticket if exists.
2) Check control plane health: https://console.redwood.internal/overview -> look for provisioning errors.
3) Get cluster state: kubectl -n inference-prod get pods -o wide | egrep "Restart|CrashLoopBackOff|Evicted"
4) If ~all inference pods restarting, flag as cluster-wide coldstart. Pause autoscaler if runaway (see 'manual commands').
5) Flip traffic staging -> fallback pool if configured: redwoodctl route set --route inference-api --target dedicated-fallback --reason "coldstart bridge"

Manual commands (use with caution, run as infra-admin):
- pause autoscaler: redwoodctl autoscale suspend --pool inference-prod  (or kubectl apply -f suspend-autoscaler.yaml)
- check model servers: kubectl -n inference-prod logs deploy/model-server --tail=200 | egrep "(OOM|failed to allocate|could not load)"
- restart a single replica (probe semantics): kubectl -n inference-prod rollout restart deployment/model-server --grace-period=30
- evict and rebuild a node: kubectl drain node/<name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

KV / prefix cache priming (important after mass eviction):
- Reason: coldstart causes KV caches and language model KV caches to be empty -> first requests are slow (p99 spikes) and more expensive.
- Quick plan: identify busiest models (top-3 by last14d queries) and run warmup scripts that send short prefix requests to repopulate KV. Use low QPS wave: warmup-tool --model mX --qps 2 --duration 600s --prefixes warmup/prefix-set.json
- If using shared cache cluster, verify redis memory pressure: redis-cli INFO memory | grep used_memory_human

Observability / dashboards to watch:
- /dashboards/inference/latency-overview (watch p50/p95/p99)
- /dashboards/inference/errors (error-class breakouts, enable tag filter for "coldstart")
- /alerts: INF-CPU-High, INF-Pods-Restarts, CACHE-MISS-Rate

Fallback routing / degrade modes (fast options):
- Route low-priority traffic to cheaper but slower model variant: redwoodctl routing update --selector priority:low --model m-small-v2
- Enable synchronous fallback to hosted API for critical customers only (use feature-guard): feature-flag enable hosted-fallback --scope customer:enterprise-critical

Escalation matrix (who to ping):
- Primary SRE (on call): Aisha Kapoor (pager)
- Runtime lead: Diego Martinez (slack + phone)
- Product / Customer impact lead: Priya Nair (cc on major incidents)

Notes-to-self (freeform):
- If controller shows consistent provisioning errors, look for kernel OOMs on nodes (dmesg) and node-level OOM-kill logs.
- Avoid mass restart of controllers at once; prefer rolling restarts with 1-2 min gap.
- Warmup duration: plan for 10-20 minutes for stable p95 if KV cache is refilled.

Open questions / follow-ups to add to ticket: (copy this into INF-XXXX)
- Do we have a dedicated warmup pool we can pre-wire into autoscaling policies?
- Can product own a minimal set of canonical prefixes for priming heavy models?
- Do cost alarms need to be adjusted to avoid auto-scaling loops during coldstart?

Post-incident cleanup (short list):
- Re-enable autoscaler: redwoodctl autoscale resume --pool inference-prod (verify stable before full resume)
- Remove temporary routing/feature flags triggered during bridge.
- Add warmup job to infra-scheduler (if repeatable) and attach to ticket.
- Rough blameless notes: what repeated, where we lacked tooling, and a simple runbook improvement (e.g., one-click pause autoscale + priming job).

Personal shorthand / reminders:
- "coldstart signature" = high pod churn + empty KV + p99 spike; if two of three match, treat as coldstart.
- Default warmup qps per model: 2-5 depending on model size.
- Keep one headset open to #oncall-inference and disable notifications for non-bridge chatter.

If you expand this into a full runbook, include: precise commands for each cloud provider, IAM notes for who can run suspend/resume, and a templated slack bridge message with incident link and ticket.

-- Marcos
(append this note to INF ticket and ping Aisha if you're stepping off)
